about.title: Glendale Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Glendale sits where two freeways meet, and that shapes how crashes happen here. SR-134 carries commuters across the top of the city while I-5 runs along its western edge, and public records list both among the corridors with the most reported collisions. Off the freeways, Brand Boulevard and San Fernando Road account for a large share of the rest. In 2025, the most recent finalized year, Glendale recorded 727 injury collisions, 978 people injured, and 3 traffic deaths across a city of about 201,000 residents. Reports cluster on Tuesday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m., the same window when many people are heading home. If one of those numbers is you, the paperwork can feel heavier than the injury. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect you with an independent personal injury attorney in Los Angeles County who handles car accident claims on contingency, so nothing is owed unless there is a recovery. You get a straight answer about your options before you speak with the other driver's insurer.

items.title: Deadlines that vary by defendant
items.desc: California gives most car accident victims two years to file, but a claim involving a city vehicle, Caltrans road condition, or other government entity can require a notice within six months. An attorney can sort out which clock applies to your crash before it runs.

items.title: Partial fault does not end your claim
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can recover even if you shared some blame; your award is simply reduced by your percentage. Insurers often overstate that percentage, which is one reason to avoid giving them a recorded statement early.

items.title: No cap, no upfront fee
items.desc: California places no ceiling on non-economic damages like pain and lost quality of life in an ordinary car accident case. The attorneys in our network take these matters on contingency, so you pay nothing unless there is a recovery.

items.question: I was hit on the 134 near the Brand Boulevard exit. Does it matter that it happened on a freeway?
items.answer: For most crashes, the location changes the evidence more than the law. Freeway collisions on SR-134 or I-5 are usually handled by the California Highway Patrol rather than Glendale police, so your report comes from a different agency. If a road defect or a government-owned vehicle played a role, a much shorter six-month notice period can apply, which makes early review worthwhile.

items.question: The other driver's insurer keeps calling for a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: You are not required to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company, and it is generally wise to decline until you have spoken with an attorney. Adjusters use those recordings to assign you a larger share of fault under comparative negligence. Keep your own notes, photos, and medical records instead, and let a lawyer handle the conversation.

items.question: What does it cost to get connected through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free matching service, not a law firm, and we do not charge you at any stage. The independent attorney you are connected with works on contingency, meaning their fee comes only out of a recovery, and you owe nothing if there is none.
